issues.legal_issue: A property-character finding based on interpretation of a grant and a prior judgment is a mixed question of law and fact that may be considered by the High Court in an estate-duty reference.
material_facts: The revenue authority treated the properties as the deceased office-holder’s personal property after considering the terms of the grant and a prior civil judgment about the properties.
The High Court considered those materials and concluded that the properties belonged to the religious institution.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could consider the nature and character of the properties because the revenue authority’s conclusion was not a pure finding of fact.
issues.legal_principle: In a reference, the High Court ordinarily answers the question on the facts found by the tribunal and does not interfere with a pure finding of fact without a specific question challenging it. But a conclusion about the character of property reached by interpreting a grant and considering a prior judgment is a mixed question of law and fact. The Court considered Karnani Properties Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income Tax, West Bengal, and Commissioner of Income Tax, Poona v. Manna Ramji & Co. in addressing the limits on review of factual findings.

predicates.estate_duty_reference: The matter came before the High Court as a reference concerning an estate-duty assessment.
predicates.tribunal_property_finding_based_on_inter: The revenue authority characterized the property by interpreting the grant and considering a prior judgment.

issues.definition: When an estate-duty reference involves a property finding based on interpreting a grant and a prior judgment, the High Court may determine the property’s character.

issues.legal_issue: Estate duty is not chargeable on trust property of a religious institution when the deceased office-holder had no property he could dispose of and no particular beneficial interest passed on death.
material_facts: The properties had been granted for the benefit of a religious institution, and a prior civil judgment had found that they belonged to the institution rather than to the office-holder personally.
The grant restricted the disposal or transfer of the properties.
The office-holder was selected according to the institution’s custom, and the properties did not pass to his heirs by inheritance.
The deceased office-holder enjoyed the properties in common with the institution’s disciples but had no particular or specific beneficial interest in them.
After his death, a successor selected according to custom took charge; the deceased’s right of common enjoyment did not pass to that successor or to another person.
issues.conclusion: No estate duty was payable on the institutional properties because the deceased had no property competent to dispose of and no interest passed to another person on his death.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 6 of the Estate Duty Act, property that the deceased was competent to dispose of is deemed to pass on death. Under section 7(1), an interest ceasing on death is deemed to pass only to the extent that a benefit accrues or arises from its cessation; section 7(4) excludes an interest held only as the holder of an office or as recipient of the benefit of a charity. Section 2(16) defines property passing on death to include property passing immediately or after an interval. On the facts, the office-holder had no disposable property or particular beneficial interest, and his common enjoyment ceased without passing to another person.

rule.if: estate_duty_assessment_on_death and property_belongs_to_religious_institution and deceased_had_no_disposable_property and deceased_had_only_common_enjoyment_as_office_holder and deceased_interest_did_not_pass_to_another_person

predicates.estate_duty_assessment_on_death: The proceeding concerns an assessment of duty on property said to pass when a person dies.
predicates.property_belongs_to_religious_institutio: The property belongs to a religious institution rather than to the person who held its office.
predicates.deceased_had_no_disposable_property: The deceased had no property that he was competent to dispose of.
predicates.deceased_had_only_common_enjoyment_as_of: The deceased’s only interest in the property was common enjoyment connected with holding an office.
predicates.deceased_interest_did_not_pass_to_anothe: The deceased’s interest ceased at death and did not pass to the successor or any other person.

issues.definition: When an estate-duty assessment concerns institutional property, the deceased had no disposable property, held only common enjoyment as an office-holder, and that interest did not pass to another person, duty is not chargeable on the institutional property.
